Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Sun Pharma's Q2 FY27 Financial Results 
Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the 
conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star and then zero on your touchtone phone. Please note that 
this conference is being recorded. 
I now hand the conference over to Dr. Abhishek Sharma, Vice President and Head of Investor Relations and 
Strategic Projects. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Abhishek Sharma: Thank you. Good evening, and a warm welcome to our second quarter FY27 earnings call. 
I'm Abhishek from the Sun Pharma Investor Relations team. We hope you have received the Q2 financials, the 
press release and the earnings presentation that was sent out earlier in the day. These are also available on our 
website. 
We have with us Mr. Dilip Shanghvi, Chairman; Mr. Kirti Ganorkar, Managing Director; Ms. Jayashree 
Satagopan, CFO; and Mr. Richard Ascroft, CEO, North America. Today, the team will provide an update on the 
financial performance and business highlights for the quarter, pipeline updates and respond to any questions that 
you may have. We will refer to the consolidated financials during management comments. The call recording and 
call transcript will also be put on our website shortly. 
The Organon acquisition is subject to satisfaction of the remaining customary closing conditions and is on track 
to close by early 2027. Organon has already announced their corresponding quarter results. Since Organon 
remains a separate public listed company, we will not be taking any questions today regarding Organon's business 
performance. 
The discussion today might include certain forward-looking statements, and these must be viewed in conjunction 
with the risks that our business faces. You are requested to ask two questions in the initial round. I also request 
all of you to kindly send in your questions that may remain unanswered today. 
I will now hand over the call to our CFO, Ms. Jayashree Satagopan. 
Jayashree Satagopan: Welcome, and thank you all for joining us for the earnings call after the announcement of 
the financial results for the second quarter FY27. The financials are already with you. Let me take you through 
the key consolidated financials. During the second quarter of FY27, sales were at INR1,61,000 million, registering 
a growth of 11.8% vis-a-vis Q2 FY26. Gross margin was at 80.8% for the quarter, higher than the same period 
last year, largely on account of a better product mix and favorable currency tailwinds.

EBITDA for the quarter was INR47,439 million, an increase of 4.8% over Q2 last year. EBITDA margins came 
in at 29.3%. EBITDA margins are lower year-on-year. Please note that Q2 FY26 had some benefit from

Forex gain for the quarter was INR785 million, which is lower than Q2 of last year. Reported net profit after tax 
for Q2 FY27 was INR19,885 million, while adjusted net profit for the quarter was INR31,620 million. EPS for 
the quarter was INR8.3 per share. Exceptional items for the second quarter includes provision towards a litigation 
settlement and on account of Organon-related acquisition costs. Effective tax rate for the quarter was 28.3% versus 
24.7% in Q2 FY26. Balance sheet continues to be strong with a net cash of USD3.3 billion at the consolidated 
level. 
Now let me take you through the half yearly performance. For the first half, sales were at INR3,12,836 million, 
registering a growth of 11% over the first half last year. Gross margin was at 80.6% for the first half. EBITDA 
for the first half was INR91,616 million, registering a growth of 3.8% over the first half of last year. EBITDA 
margin percentage was at 29.1%. 
Adjusted net profit for H1 was INR62,515 million. The successful subscription of Sun Pharma's debut NCD issue 
underscores the strength of its credit profile and the broad investor confidence in the company's financial position. 
I will now hand it over to Kirti, who will share the performance of our Global Innovative Medicines business and 
India business. 
Kirti Ganorkar: Thank you, Jayashree. I shall first provide you an update on Global Innovative Medicine. In Q2 
FY27, our Innovative Medicines sales were up 6.9% to reach USD356 million. The business accounted for 21.1% 
of Sun sales for the quarter. The performance in Innovative Medicine continues to be driven by growth across US 
and ex-US market across products, notably Ilumya, ex-US, Cequa, Odomzo. 
We are pleased to note that Ilumya is now approved in the US for the treatment of adults with active psoriatic 
arthritis. Introducing a health care provider-administered IL-23 inhibitor broadens our treatment portfolio and 
creates new opportunities to strengthen patient support and health care team engagement. We are planning for a 
soft launch in November with a full launch in the following months. 
Ilumya continues to do well across international markets. As a highlight, recently, Japanese Society for Psoriasis 
Research announced that Ilumya to be number 2 across all biologics in the new patient across 73 main hospitals 
in Japan, making a significant improvement over last year. During the quarter, partnership with LIB Therapeutics 
strengthened our innovative medicine portfolio and expanded our presence in the rapidly growing PCSK9 market

SMSRC March-June '26 report, we continue to be number 1 company based on prescription volumes. Sun Pharma 
is also ranked number 1 by prescription with 12 different doctor categories. For Q2 FY27, the company launched 
15 new products in India. 
Regarding Organon, integration planning for the Organon acquisition continues to progress across functions and 
work streams in line with plan. Regulatory approvals have now been secured in majority of the regions with the 
remaining jurisdiction tracking on schedule. We are now on track to close the transaction as per earlier 
communicated timelines, that is Q4 of FY27. 
I will now hand over the call to Rick for update on the US market. 
Richard Ascroft: Thank you, Kirti. Let me share performance highlights for our US business. Overall, the US 
business reported sales of USD455 million for the quarter, declining by 8.2%. This decline is largely due to 
lenalidomide erosion. On a quarter-over-quarter basis, the US business has grown by 6.5%. The US accounted 
for 27% of consolidated sales for the quarter, and we launched 5 generic products, in the US during this quarter. 
This quarter, we saw a slowdown in Ilumya business in the US driven by a mix of factors. This is a key reason 
behind slower growth in global innovative medicines. We put actions in place to improve performance and 
anticipate further growth from these as well as the new psoriatic arthritis indication that Kirti mentioned earlier. 
The rest of our Innovative Medicines portfolio in the US continues to show strong growth. 
I also want to provide some recent updates on Unloxcyt. Unloxcyt's elevation to a Category 2A preferred 
recommendation in the NCCN guidelines reinforces its growing clinical relevance in advanced CSCC. 
Subsequently, we presented long-term follow-up data on Unloxcyt at a leading scientific conference in Europe. 
Long-term data showed complete responses in 34% of locally advanced and 17% to 21% of metastatic patients

Kunal Dhamesha: First one on the slowdown in growth for Ilumya in US Rick, can you highlight what is driving
